lines.japanese: そのあと店の中を探してみたものの日和子さんは見つかりませんでした。
lines.english: Afterward, I searched the restaurant, but Hiyoko was nowhere to be found.

lines.japanese: 本当は外にも探しに行きたいけど、これから混雑するって時間に俺まで居なくなるわけいかないし……ああでも、マスターには日和子さんのことを言っておいた方がいいよなあ。
lines.english: What I really wanted was to search outside. But I couldn't abandon the restaurant just as the evening rush was beginning... Still, I ought to tell the boss about Hiyoko.

lines.japanese: パスタセットを運びながら、同じことを何度も何度も考えていました。
lines.english: I turned the same thoughts over and over as I carried a pasta set across the floor.

lines.japanese: ああ、そういえば占いの館のこともあったんだった。
lines.english: Oh, right. There was the fortune-telling parlor too.

lines.japanese: 今日はブルボンヌ冴子さんこと、沢井さんの出勤日。
lines.english: Today was a working day for Sawai, otherwise known as Madame Saeko Bourbonne.

lines.japanese: 今日を逃すと、次のシフトは月曜日なんだっけ。時間も２２時までのシフトだったし。
lines.english: If I missed tonight, her next shift wouldn't be until Monday. And tonight she was working until ten.

lines.japanese: てことはどのみち勤務時間中だから無理ってことかあ。さて、どうしましょう。
lines.english: Which meant I couldn't go anyway, because I would still be working. So what was I supposed to do?

lines.japanese: 「やっぽーん！　千歳くん、こっちこっちー！」
lines.english: “Yoo-hoo! Chitose! Over here!”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ」
lines.english: “Oh!”

lines.japanese: パスタセットをご注文のお客様は紀奈子さんでした。ああそんな、フォークとスプーンを持って子どもみたいに机を叩いて……。
lines.english: The customer who had ordered the pasta set was Kinako. Oh, honestly. She had a fork in one hand and a spoon in the other and was drumming them on the table like a child.

lines.japanese: 「お待たせしました。来てたんですか紀奈子さん」
lines.english: “Sorry to keep you waiting. I didn't know you were here, Kinako.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、来てたんだけど千歳くんもいないし、えりちゃんもひよちゃんもいないから退屈してたとこなんさ」
lines.english: “Yep. But you weren't around, and neither were Eri or Hiyo, so I was getting bored.”

lines.japanese: 「や、あの紀奈子さん、俺たち仕事中なんすけど」
lines.english: “Um, Kinako, we are at work.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、冷たーい。だって千歳くんも、店員だった私でかなーり遊んでたよ？」
lines.english: “Aw, so cold. You had plenty of fun with me back when I was a waitress.”

lines.japanese: 「分かりました。そんなにおっしゃるなら、紀奈子さんのパスタを黄な粉まみれにして遊んであげましょう。いま厨房からくすねてきます」
lines.english: “Very well. If you insist, I'll entertain you by burying your pasta in soybean flour. I'll go steal some from the kitchen.”

lines.japanese: 「ああうぅ！　待って千歳君、パスタにかけるならせめてチーズかタバスコにしようよ、国境を超えちゃダメ」
lines.english: “Nooo! Wait, Chitose. If you're putting something on pasta, at least make it cheese or Tabasco. Don't cross international borders.”

lines.japanese: 「だったらパルメザン望月か望月タバス子に改名してください。ダジャレが成りたちません」
lines.english: “Then change your name to Parmesan Mochizuki or Tabasco Mochizuki. Otherwise the pun doesn't work.”

lines.japanese: 「うう、今日の千歳君はなんだかノリが悪いなあ。好きなひとが出来たからって、他の子に冷たくなるのはよくないよ？」
lines.english: “Aww. You're not much fun today, Chitose. Just because you've found someone you like doesn't mean you should turn cold to every other girl.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それでひよちゃんは？」
lines.english: “Oh, by the way, where's Hiyo?”

lines.japanese: 「あの、今の会話の流れで自然にひよちゃんの名前を出すのやめてください」
lines.english: “Please don't work Hiyo's name into the conversation quite so naturally after saying that.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　また怒られたりした？」
lines.english: “Hmm? Did she scold you again?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それがですねえ……」
lines.english: “Well, actually…”

lines.japanese: んー、この状況をどう説明するべきかな。でも紀奈子さんって俺と同じ立場にいたひとだから、俺の気持ちを分かってくれるんじゃないかなあ。
lines.english: Hmm. How was I supposed to explain the situation? Still, Kinako had once stood where I did now. Perhaps she would understand how I felt.

lines.japanese: 「そうですね、聞いてください紀奈子さん。アナタ亡きあとのこの店の惨状を」
lines.english: “All right, listen to this, Kinako. Let me describe the wretched state of this restaurant since your untimely passing.”

lines.japanese: 「今まで緩衝材の苦労なんて考えたこともなかったんですけどね。適当にぷちぷち言ってればいいもんだと思っていたらとんでもない。もうぶちりと一息に潰されそうです」
lines.english: “I never appreciated how hard it was to be the bubble wrap around here. I thought all you had to do was sit in the middle going pop, pop. I was wrong. At this rate, somebody's going to crush me in one squeeze.”

lines.japanese: 「潰されるの？」
lines.english: “You’re being crushed?”

lines.japanese: 「潰されます。潰されまくってます」
lines.english: “Constantly. Mercilessly.”

lines.japanese: 「挟まれてるの？」
lines.english: “Caught in the middle?”

lines.japanese: 「挟まれてます。千歳ぷちぷち鷲介です」
lines.english: “Right in the middle. Shusuke Pop-Pop Chitose, at your service.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ。千歳君がんばってくれてるんだね」
lines.english: “Hee hee. You’ve been working hard, haven’t you?”

lines.japanese: 紀奈子さんはしみじみとうなずく俺を見て、この世の全てを癒してくれるかのような笑顔になりました。
lines.english: As I nodded with grave feeling, Kinako gave me a smile that seemed capable of healing every sorrow in the world.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ありがとうございます。そうです、この苦悩を分かってくれるのは同じ土俵で戦ってきた紀奈子さんだけなんです」
lines.english: “Th-thank you. Yes, the only one who understands my torment is Kinako, who once fought in this very ring.”

lines.japanese: 「だって私もう部外者だもん。聞くだけならなんでも聞くよ」
lines.english: “But I'm an outsider now. I'll listen to anything you want to say.”

lines.japanese: 「聞くだけなんだ！」
lines.english: “You’ll only listen!?”

lines.japanese: 「でも逃げずに立ち向かってるからえらいよ。千歳くん、ちょっと変わった？」
lines.english: “Still, you're doing well to stand your ground instead of running away. Have you changed a little, Chitose?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、そう見えますか」
lines.english: “Oh? Does it look that way?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、もう立派なアレキサンダーの一員だね」
lines.english: “Yes. You're a proper member of Alexander now.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、毎日が楽しいですよ」
lines.english: “Every day is a delight.”

lines.japanese: 「ちぇー、私も千歳くんがいる間にアルバイトに戻りたいなー」
lines.english: “Darn. I wish I could come back and work here while you're still around.”
“Wonderful!”

lines.japanese: 「さすがです紀奈子さん！　受験二ヶ月前だというのに、職場という名のレジャースポットに思いを馳せるその横向き思考！　追いつめられていても、気持ちの切り替え方を心得ている！」
lines.english: “That's our Kinako! Two months before her entrance exams, and she's daydreaming about that vacation paradise called work! Even with her back to the wall, she knows how to turn her mind ninety degrees and escape!”

lines.japanese: 「うん。だって気持ちを切り替えたくてここに来てるんだもん」
lines.english: “Yep. I came here because I wanted to switch tracks.”

lines.japanese: 「今日もお母さんとケンカしてきちゃってさ。それでここに逃げてきたんだ」
lines.english: “I had another fight with Mom today, so I ran away here.”

lines.japanese: 「え、仏の紀奈子の異名をとるアナタでもケンカとかするんですか」
lines.english: “What? Even Kinako the Merciful gets into fights?”

lines.japanese: 「するよー！　もー、今日だって受験のことで揉めちゃって、ケータイにつばをぺぺぺと飛ばしてきたぞ」
lines.english: “Of course I do! We argued about my exams again today, and I sprayed spit all over my phone—ptoo, ptoo, ptoo.”

lines.japanese: 「へーえ、なんか意外っていうか、想像できない光景っすねそれ」
lines.english: “Huh. That’s unexpected. I can’t even picture it.”

lines.japanese: 「ケータイに涙をぺぺぺと飛ばしてきたぞ」
lines.english: “I sprayed tears all over my phone—splat, splat, splat.”

lines.japanese: 「あらら、お母さん厳しい人なんすか？」
lines.english: “Oh dear. Is your mother strict?”

lines.japanese: 「んー？　性格はよく似てるって言われるけど」
lines.english: “Hmm? People say our personalities are very similar.”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さんが誰かとケンカする要素ないすよね。紀奈子さんが言い争いしてるトコなんて見たことないですよ？」
lines.english: “But you just don't seem like someone who gets into fights. I've never seen you argue with anybody.”

lines.japanese: 「そう？　私は言うときは言うよー。お母さんも譲らないからすぐケンカになるんだ」
lines.english: “Really? I speak my mind when it matters. Mom refuses to give an inch too, so we start fighting in no time.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうなんすか。言うときは言っちゃうひとなんすか」
lines.english: “I-is that so? You’re the type to speak your mind?”

lines.japanese: 「言う言う。お互いにわんわん泣き出しちゃって、わけ分からなくなるときだってあるもん」
lines.english: “Absolutely. Sometimes we both start bawling until neither of us knows what's going on anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「わんわん……」
lines.english: “Bawling…”

lines.japanese: そんなことを言う目の前の紀奈子さんは、にこにこと微笑んでいました。
lines.english: Kinako spoke of it with her usual warm smile.

lines.japanese: 「でも紀奈子さんって、ここで働いてたときは調停役でしたよね？」
lines.english: “But when you worked here, you were always the peacemaker, weren’t you?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ、どこに言ってもわがまま言ってわんわん泣いてたら、私ただのおかしいひとだよ」
lines.english: “Well, if I went everywhere making selfish demands and bawling my eyes out, I'd just be a crazy person.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……そうっすねえ。人間誰しも家や職場や学校で、それぞれキャラ違いますもんね」
lines.english: “True enough... Everyone acts a little different at home, at work, and at school.”

lines.japanese: 「でしょ？　それに一人でずっと勉強してると、受験の日が近いこととか三回目で後がないことも不安になっちゃって、すーぐここに逃げてきちゃうんだ」
lines.english: “Exactly. And when I study alone too long, I start thinking about how close the exam is, and how this is my third try and there won't be another. Then I come running here.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなにアレキサンダーは落ちつきますか」
lines.english: “Does Alexander calm you down that much?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。だって毎日来てるからねー」
lines.english: “Yep. I come every day, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「バイトしてたときと変わらないじゃん！」
lines.english: “That’s no different from when you worked here!”

lines.japanese: そういえば俺が入ってからというもの、ほとんど毎日紀奈子さんと顔を合わせている気がします。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I felt as though I had seen Kinako nearly every day since I started.

lines.japanese: 「だから私いつも言ってるでしょ、逃げ腰は癖になっちゃうって」
lines.english: “That's why I'm always telling you: once you start running away, it becomes a habit.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな悩みがあるなら言ってくださいよ。紀奈子さん、そんなこと顔にも出さないから分からないじゃないすか。ほら、話してくれれば俺でも元気づけてあげられるかもしれないし」
lines.english: “If you're struggling with things like that, tell me. You never let it show, so how am I supposed to know? If you talked to me, even I might be able to cheer you up.”

lines.japanese: 「んーん、気を楽にしに来てるのにそんなこと話したくないもん。千歳君は私の受験のことなんて気にしないでいつも通りにしてくれればいいんだよ」
lines.english: “No. I come here to relax, so I don't want to talk about it. Don't worry about my exams, Chitose. Just act the way you always do.”
“Hmm…”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ」
lines.english: “Hee hee.”

lines.japanese: 俺が次の言葉を考えている間に、紀奈子さんはパスタにチーズをぱぱぱとかけて食べ始めました。
lines.english: While I searched for something to say, Kinako showered her pasta with cheese and began to eat.

lines.japanese: 「おお、望月君が来ていたのか。受験勉強の方はどうだ」
lines.english: “Ah, Miss Mochizuki. I didn’t realize you were here. How go the entrance-exam preparations?”

lines.japanese: 「店長こんばんはー。はーい、行きづまっちゃったから頭をすっきりさせにきましたー」
lines.english: “Evening, Manager! My brain locked up, so I came here to clear my head.”

lines.japanese: 嬉しそうにパスタを食べる紀奈子さんは、どこから見てもいつも通りの彼女でした。
lines.english: As she happily ate her pasta, Kinako looked exactly as she always did.

lines.japanese: そりゃあ家族でもない限り分からないことだけど、紀奈子さんも俺の知らないところで戦ってたんだ。
lines.english: Unless you were family, there was no way to know. Kinako had battles of her own, fought where I could never see them.

lines.japanese: 人間いつかは戦わなくちゃいけないかなあ……。
lines.english: Perhaps everyone had to fight eventually...

lines.japanese: 「んー、そろそろ帰ろっかな」
lines.english: “Hmm. Maybe I should head home soon.”

lines.japanese: 三人で雑談をしていたら、紀奈子さんが時計を見ながら言いました。
lines.english: After the three of us had chatted for a while, Kinako glanced at the clock.

lines.japanese: 「もうちょっと話したかったけど、そろそろ受験勉強を再開だい」
lines.english: “I wanted to talk a little longer, but it's time to get back to studying.”

lines.japanese: 「そうか。なんなら俺が夜の受験勉強を付きっきりで教えても構わないが」
lines.english: “I see. If you like, I could stay by your side all night and give you some very private exam coaching.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、今日は寄りたいお店があるからいいです」
lines.english: “Hmm. There’s a shop I want to visit tonight, so no, thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「なかったらやるんすか、夜の受験勉強」
lines.english: “Would you accept his private coaching if you didn't have plans?”

lines.japanese: 「むっ、もしかして三丁目の『私立ぬるぬる女学院』に行くのか望月君。それなら俺も付きあうぞ」
lines.english: “Hmm? Miss Mochizuki, are you perhaps visiting the Private Slippery Women's Academy in the third district? If so, I shall accompany you.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとりで行ってください。私が行くのはグローヴ街のレッドヒールって靴屋さんです」
lines.english: “Please go by yourself. I’m going to Red Heel, the shoe store on Grove Street.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　あ、そこって……」
lines.english: “What? Oh, that’s…”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、千歳くん知ってるんだ。女ものの靴屋さんなのによく知ってたね」
lines.english: “You know it, Chitose? I'm surprised you've heard of a women's shoe store.”

lines.japanese: 行ったこともない店です。だけど俺はその名前を知っていました。沢井さんのブログで見たのです。
lines.english: I had never set foot inside. But I knew the name from Sawai's blog.

lines.japanese: その靴屋の隣りにあるという占い屋さんは、まさに近いうち訪ねたいと思っていた例の店です。
lines.english: The fortune-telling parlor beside that shoe store was the very place I intended to visit soon.

lines.japanese: 近いうち……それはいつになるのでしょう。
lines.english: Soon... but when would that be?

lines.japanese: 「あの、マスター」
lines.english: “Um, boss?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どうした」
lines.english: “Hmm? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「その、日和子さんっていまどこに……」
lines.english: “Do you know where Hiyoko is right now…?”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 俺の声に気付いたのか、マスターはおどけた仮面を外し、ごく稀に見せる頼もしい大人の顔になりました。
lines.english: Perhaps he heard the concern in my voice. The boss let his fool's mask fall away and showed the dependable face of a grown man—a face I saw only rarely.

lines.japanese: 「それは、俺がおまえに聞こうと思っていたことだ。玉泉君ならさっき仕事着のまま外へ飛びだしていったが、なにかあったのか」
lines.english: “I was about to ask you the same thing. Miss Tamaizumi ran outside earlier, still in her work uniform. Did something happen?”
“Oh, no…”

lines.japanese: そっか。日和子さん、やっぱり外に行っちゃったのか。
lines.english: So Hiyoko really had gone outside.

lines.japanese: あの真面目な子のことだから、きっと今ごろ、どこかで死ぬほど無断早退を後悔してるんだろうな。
lines.english: Knowing how earnest she was, she was probably somewhere out there regretting walking off the job with every fiber of her being.

lines.japanese: 「千歳君、なにかあったんなら話してよ。ひよちゃんの力になりたいのは、千歳君だけじゃないんだからね」
lines.english: “Chitose, if something happened, tell us. You aren't the only one who wants to help Hiyo.”

lines.japanese: 俺は少し考えたあと、さっきの出来事を話すことにしました。
lines.english: After thinking for a moment, I decided to explain what had happened.

lines.japanese: 「実はさっき、日和子さんと英里子さんがトラブって言い争いになっちゃったんすよ」
lines.english: “Actually, Hiyoko and Eriko got into it earlier. It turned into an argument.”

lines.japanese: 「そのときに、言葉の弾みで日和子さんの三作目の話になって――」
lines.english: “In the heat of the moment, the subject of Hiyoko’s third book came up—”

lines.japanese: なんだか告げ口をしているみたいで嫌な気持ちもありましたが、事の解決には二人の力を借りないといけなそうです。
lines.english: I hated the feeling that I was telling tales behind their backs. But resolving the situation would likely require both their help.

lines.japanese: 俺は思いきって、自分が抱えていることを全て話してみることにしました。
lines.english: I gathered my courage and told them everything weighing on me.

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、えりちゃんが！？　もーっ、ダメだよえりちゃん、私ちょっと叱ってくる」
lines.english: “What? Eri did that!? Honestly, Eri! I'm going to give her a piece of my mind.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いやいや、それが英里子さんが悪いってわけでもないんです」
lines.english: “No, wait. It isn't as though Eriko was entirely in the wrong.”

lines.japanese: 俺は立ちあがりかけた紀奈子さんを押さえて、マスターに向きなおりました。
lines.english: I held Kinako back as she began to rise, then turned to the boss.

lines.japanese: 「どっちかっていうと問題は日和子さん自身のことっていうか……」
lines.english: “If anything, the real problem lies with Hiyoko herself...”

lines.japanese: 「こんなこと勝手に話して怒られるかもしれないんですけど、日和子さん三作目を書きあげたんですよ」
lines.english: “She might be angry with me for telling you this without permission, but Hiyoko finished her third book.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう」
lines.english: “Oh?”

lines.japanese: 「ほほー！」
lines.english: “Oho!”

lines.japanese: あ、喜んでくれてる。日和子さんのことだけど嬉しいなあ。
lines.english: They were happy for her. It was Hiyoko's achievement, but somehow their delight warmed me too.

lines.japanese: 「で、その提出した原稿がどんな感じか、こっそり米田さんに聞いてみたんすよ」
lines.english: “So I secretly asked Yoneda what had happened to the manuscript after Hiyoko submitted it.”

lines.japanese: 「そしたら、日和子さんの担当さん、読みもせずに放ったらかしみたいで……」
lines.english: “Apparently her editor hasn't even read it. She's simply left it sitting there...”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ、そんなあ……」
lines.english: “What? That’s awful…”

lines.japanese: 「ホント内容はいいものなんですよ。まあ、だから本になるとも限らないんでしょうけど、とにかく結果だけでも出れば日和子さんの心も決まると思うんです」
lines.english: “The book itself really is good. Of course that doesn't guarantee publication, but if Hiyoko could at least get an answer, I think she'd finally know what she wants to do.”

lines.japanese: 「そうすれば英里子さんとも少しは向かいあえるのかなと思って……だから俺、なんとかしてその担当さんに原稿を読んでもらいたいんです」
lines.english: “Then perhaps she could face Eriko a little more honestly too... That's why I want to find some way to get her editor to read the manuscript.”

lines.japanese: 「なんとかって？」
lines.english: “Some way?”

lines.japanese: 「まあその、直談判とか？」
lines.english: “Well… a direct appeal?”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、直接編集部にでも行くつもりか。そんなことしたら逆効果になるぞ」
lines.english: “Hold on. You aren't planning to walk into the editorial department, are you? That would only backfire.”

lines.japanese: 「ですよね。ええ、ですから、編集部の外で仕掛けようかと思って。実は俺、そのひとが別の場所でアルバイトしてるのを見ちゃったんです」
lines.english: “Right. That's why I thought I might approach her away from the office. The truth is, I discovered that she works part-time somewhere else.”

lines.japanese: 「それが運よくっていうか、占い師の副業なんてしてるもんだから。客として会話をしながら、それとなく原稿を読みたくなるような方向へ誘導したいんです」
lines.english: “As luck would have it, she moonlights as a fortune-teller. I want to speak with her as a customer and subtly guide the conversation until she feels inclined to read the manuscript.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーむ」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: マスターが顎に伸びた無精ヒゲをさすりながらうなずきました。
lines.english: The boss nodded, stroking the stubble on his chin.

lines.japanese: 「なるほど、このままでは玉泉君と日野君の軋轢が激しくなり業務に支障、いや引いてはアレキサンダーの危機に繋がるな。嫌だ嫌だ、俺はおっぱいがいっぺんに二つもなくなるのは嫌だ」
lines.english: “I see. If this continues, the friction between Miss Tamaizumi and Miss Hino will intensify and impair their duties—nay, it may place Alexander itself in peril. No, no. I refuse to lose two breasts at once.”

lines.japanese: 「マスター、おっぱいは二つでワンセットですよ」
lines.english: “Boss, breasts come two to a set.”

lines.japanese: マスターはいつもの彼らしい神妙な調子で俺の目を見ると、カウベルのかかったアレキサンダーの入り口を指さしました。
lines.english: The boss looked me in the eye with his customary solemn gravity, then pointed toward Alexander's cowbell-hung entrance.

lines.japanese: 「おい鷲介、ひとっ走り行ってさっさと解決してこい」
lines.english: “Shusuke, run over there and sort this out. Now.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええ？　あの、俺まだ勤務時間中なんすけど行っていいんすか」
lines.english: “W-wait. I’m still in the middle of my shift. Are you sure I can leave?”

lines.japanese: バイトの身からは言いにくかったことを、都合よく店長が切りだしてくれたので、思わず聞きかえしてしまいました。
lines.english: As a mere part-timer, I could hardly have asked to leave myself. Now the Manager had conveniently raised the subject for me, and I found myself asking again.

lines.japanese: 「鷲介、よく考えろ。望月君がいない今、アレキサンダーのおっぱいは誰の手にかかっていると思っている。ここで玉泉君を失うわけにはいかん」
lines.english: “Think carefully, Shusuke. With Miss Mochizuki gone, in whose hands do you imagine the breasts of Alexander now rest? We cannot afford to lose Miss Tamaizumi.”

lines.japanese: 俺は思わず自分の手を見て、マスターいわくアレキサンダー花水木通り店を支えているという豊かな感触を思いだしました。
lines.english: My eyes dropped involuntarily to my hands, and I remembered the generous softness that, according to the boss, now sustained Alexander's Hanamizuki Street branch.

lines.japanese: 「あのおっぱいを手にかけるようなやつがいたら俺がやっつけてやる」
lines.english: “If anyone lays a hand on those breasts, I shall strike him down myself.”

lines.japanese: 「ああああのう！　はい、じゃあその……お言葉に甘えて行ってきます」
lines.english: “U-um! Yes, then… I’ll accept your kind offer and go.”

lines.japanese: 「うむ。おまえも玉泉君も早退扱いにしておこう。もう夜番の連中も入ってることだし、あとのことは心配しなくていいからな」
lines.english: “Indeed. I shall record both you and Miss Tamaizumi as having left early. The evening staff have already arrived, so you need not worry about matters here.”

lines.japanese: 「すみません、ご迷惑おかけします。この穴埋めはいずれ」
lines.english: “I’m sorry for the trouble. I’ll make it up to you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそうだ、占い屋なんてところへ赴くにはムサい野郎がひとりより、カップルの方が自然だろう、望月君、場所も知っているようだし力を貸してやってくれないか」
lines.english: “One more thing. A couple will look more natural visiting a fortune-teller than one disreputable man alone. Miss Mochizuki, since you appear to know the location, would you lend him your assistance?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえあの、受験で忙しい紀奈子さんにまでそんな」
lines.english: “Oh, but Kinako is already busy with her exams. I couldn’t ask her to—”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、私にも手伝わせて千歳君。一日ぐらい潰れたって全然問題ないよ。だって、ひよちゃんのためだもん！」
lines.english: “No, let me help, Chitose. Losing one day won't matter at all. This is for Hiyo!”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さん……」
lines.english: “Kinako…”

lines.japanese: なんていいひとなんだろう。
lines.english: What a wonderful person.

lines.japanese: 「どうせ暇だったしね」
lines.english: “I didn't have anything else to do anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さん……」
lines.english: “Kinako…”

lines.japanese: もうちょっと勉強してください……。
lines.english: Please study a little more...

lines.japanese: 「ふむ。しかし敵地へ潜入となると変装した方がいいな」
lines.english: “Hmm. But if you are infiltrating enemy territory, disguises would be prudent.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なんすかそれ、べつにスパイごっこじゃないんだから必要ないでしょう」
lines.english: “What? This isn’t a game of spies. We don’t need disguises.”

lines.japanese: 「何を言う。万が一、細川玉木の関係者だと知れたら説得力はゼロ、計画がすべて水の泡だ」
lines.english: “Nonsense. If she discovers your connection to Tamaki Hosokawa, your powers of persuasion will vanish and the entire plan come to nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、たしかに」
lines.english: “Oh, that’s true.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうですけど、まず占いしてもらうだけなのにそんな細かいトコばれる要素がないっすよ」
lines.english: “Technically, yes. But we're only going for a fortune-telling session. There's no reason she would uncover a detail that obscure.”

lines.japanese: 「うるさい、余計な皮を挟むな。なら鷲介はそのままでいい。その代わり望月君、君だけでも、俺のコレクションの中から一着持っていきなさい。きっと役に立つだろう」
lines.english: “Quiet. Keep your extra foreskin out of this. Fine, Shusuke can go as he is. But Miss Mochizuki, you should choose an outfit from my collection. I'm sure it will prove useful.”

lines.japanese: 「あのうマスター、せっかく紀奈子さんが協力してくれるって言ってるんだから、そんなやる気を削ぐようなこと……」
lines.english: “Boss, Kinako has generously offered to help. Please don't say something that will kill her enthusiasm...”

lines.japanese: 「店長ー、この服で私に合うサイズないですかー」
lines.english: “Manager, do you have this outfit in my size?”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！　やる気が上昇してる！？」
lines.english: “What!? That made her more enthusiastic?!”

lines.japanese: 「待ちなさい望月君。いま君が手にしているアイドル風ひらひら衣装も似合うとは思うのだが、それは占い屋の客としては不自然──」
lines.english: “Wait, Miss Mochizuki. I believe that frilly idol costume would suit you, but it would look strange on a customer at a fortune-telling parlor—”

lines.japanese: 「──よし、この言い方なら傷つけずに済むな。あー、待ちなさい望月君、いま手にしている年甲斐もないアイドル風」
lines.english: “—yes, that should spare her feelings. Ahem. Wait, Miss Mochizuki. That age-inappropriate idol costume in your hands—”

lines.japanese: 「予習した意味ないだろ？」
lines.english: “Then what was the point of rehearsing?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、まーそっすね、この中から選ぶなら学生服が一番自然なんじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Hmm. Well, if we have to choose from these, a school uniform would look the most natural.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ほんと？　私まだセーラーとかブレザーとか全然イケる？」
lines.english: “Oh, really? You think I can still pull off a sailor-style uniform or a school blazer?”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介、あくまで設定上の恋人なのだから、挿入以上のことはするなよ」
lines.english: “Shusuke, remember that she is only your girlfriend for the purposes of the cover story. Do nothing beyond penetration.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、むしろそれ以上の行為が思いつかないんすけど」
lines.english: “What the hell is beyond penetration?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえら私の質問に答えろよ」
lines.english: “Will you two answer my question?”

lines.japanese: 「すみません、勉強しなくちゃいけないのに付きあわせちゃって」
lines.english: “Sorry for dragging you along when you ought to be studying.”

lines.japanese: 俺は紀奈子さんと一緒に夜のグローヴ通りを並んで歩きました。
lines.english: Kinako and I walked side by side through Grove Street at night.

lines.japanese: 「ううん、いい息抜きになって楽しいよー」
lines.english: “No, this is a nice break. I’m having fun.”

lines.japanese: 気を使うということなど忘れさせてくれるような笑顔。このほんわかさって紀奈子さんの徳だよなあ。
lines.english: Her smile made it easy to forget I was asking a favor. That gentle warmth was one of Kinako's gifts.

lines.japanese: 「てかべつに、制服までは着なくてもいんすよ。そんな狩男のお遊びに付きあわなくても」
lines.english: “You really don't have to wear the uniform. There's no reason to indulge Karuo's games.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、でも制服を着る機会って、もうないだろうしなー」
lines.english: “Hmm. But I probably won’t have another chance to wear a school uniform.”

lines.japanese: 紀奈子さんの右手にはご自分のトートバッグと、どこかのブランドロゴが入ったビニール製のショップ袋。中身は蒼穹女学院とかいうところの冬季用制服です。
lines.english: In Kinako's right hand were her own tote bag and a plastic shopping bag bearing some brand logo. Inside lay the winter uniform of a school called Azure Sky Girls' Academy.

lines.japanese: 「私行ってたトコの制服、上下紺の普通ぅーで地味ぃーなジャンスカだったから、一度こういう都会的な制服着てみたかったんさー」
lines.english: “The uniform at my school was just a plain, drab navy jumper dress, top to bottom. I always wanted to try on a stylish city uniform like this.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、紀奈子さんって制服似合ってたんだろうなあ。さぞかし人気あったんでしょうね」
lines.english: “I bet you looked wonderful in uniform. You must have been terribly popular.”

lines.japanese: 「うち男女別学だったから、あんまり交流自体なかったよ。放課後とか女子だけで餃子食べに行って、みんなでニンニクぷんぷんさせちゃうような青春だったかな」
lines.english: “My school kept the boys and girls separate, so we barely mixed at all. My youth was mostly packs of girls going out for dumplings after school and all coming home reeking of garlic.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、それはちょっとショック。紀奈子さんのふんわり苺ミルクなイメージが……」
lines.english: “What? That's rather shocking. What happened to my image of Kinako as soft and sweet as strawberry milk...?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うそうそ今のうそ。大ウソ。うん、ごくたまにしか食べてなかったし、みんなガーリックガーリック言ってたけど、私はニンニク抜き派だから。お酢だけでさっぱり食べるよね」
lines.english: “Oh, that was a lie. A huge lie. We only ate them once in a great while, and everyone else was mad about garlic, but I always ordered mine without it. I like them light, with vinegar alone.”

lines.japanese: 「え、酢だけなんすか。醤油とかラー油もかけません？」
lines.english: “Only vinegar? Don’t you add soy sauce or chili oil?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろんその三種混合は基本だけど、通はお酢だけで食べるんさ。素材の味を楽しむために、何も付けないのもアリだよね。そうするとこう、ニンニクの香りが鼻に抜けてねー」
lines.english: “Of course the basic sauce combines all three, but connoisseurs eat them with vinegar alone. You can even eat them plain to savor the ingredients. Then the fragrance of garlic rises right through your nose...”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、やっぱりニンニク入れるんすね」
lines.english: “Ah. So you do put garlic in them.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、入れないよ。今のはあくまで水餃子の話だもん。私が好きなのは焼き餃子だから」
lines.english: “No, I don't. I was only talking about boiled dumplings just now. I like mine pan-fried.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、餃子って言ったら焼き餃子ですよね。パリッパリのが美味いっすよね」
lines.english: “Of course. When you say dumplings, you mean pan-fried. They're delicious when the outside gets wonderfully crisp.”

lines.japanese: 「へへー、うちの地元の餃子は格別だよー？　断然おいしいから、一度ひよちゃんと一緒に行ってみなよ」
lines.english: “Heh heh. The dumplings back home are in a class of their own. They're miles better than anything here. You should take Hiyo there sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「いっすねえ。そしたら紀奈子さんが実家帰るときに合わせて、望月家に御挨拶させてもらったり──」
lines.english: “That sounds great. We could time it for one of your trips home, and I could pay my respects to the Mochizuki family—”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あー、それは……んー、いぐねっぺなー」
lines.english: “Oh. Uh... that might not be such a great idea.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そーなんすか？　ああ、そうですよね、余所者がいきなりお邪魔したいなんて図々しいっすよね」
lines.english: “Really? Oh, right. It'd be pretty presumptuous for some outsider to invite himself into your family home.”

lines.japanese: 「や、や、ごめんね。そういうことじゃないの、そうじゃなくて、私いま半勘当されてるから」
lines.english: “No, no, I'm sorry. That isn't it. It's just that I've been half disowned.”

lines.japanese: 「半、勘当？　ってなんすかそれ」
lines.english: “Half disowned? What does that mean?”

lines.japanese: 「前に話したの覚えてる？　うちの親、私の進学に反対してたって。してたって言うか、現在進行形で絶賛してりんぐ中だけど」
lines.english: “Remember what I told you? My parents were against me going to university. Or rather, they *are* against it. Very actively. Present progressive.”

lines.japanese: 「あのね、私が一人暮らししてるのって、こっちの予備校通うからってゆーよりは、お父さんに実家追いだされちゃったからなの」
lines.english: “See, I don't live alone so much because I go to prep school here as because my father threw me out of the house.”

lines.japanese: 「え、それは……ちょっとした親子喧嘩じゃなくて、リアルに？」
lines.english: “Wait. So this wasn't some minor quarrel between parent and child? He actually did?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。おばあちゃんとお姉ちゃん夫婦が味方してくれてて、お母さんは中立。だけどお父さんとおじいちゃんはリアルにぷんすかぷんで、もう二年も敷居またがせてくれないんさ」
lines.english: “Yep. Grandma and my sister and her husband are on my side, and Mom's neutral. But Dad and Grandpa are still hopping mad. They haven't let me set foot in the house for two years.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でも、たまーに里帰りしてませんでした？　そだ、お土産に苺もらってますよ俺ら」
lines.english: “But haven't you gone home sometimes? That's right—you brought all of us strawberries as a souvenir.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それは里帰りっていうか日帰り旅行だね。実家近くまでは行くことあるけど、家には入れないから」
lines.english: “That was less a homecoming than a day trip. Sometimes I go back to the area, but I'm not allowed inside the house.”

lines.japanese: 「へ、へえー……それは、なんていうか、大変すね」
lines.english: “I-I see… That sounds… difficult.”

lines.japanese: 大変ってなんだ。ボキャ貧だなあ、俺。
lines.english: *Difficult?* Was that really the best I could do? What a pitiful vocabulary.

lines.japanese: でもこんなとき、なんて返すのが正解なんでしょう。
lines.english: But what was the right response at a time like this?

lines.japanese: 「突っ込んだこと聞いちゃってすいません」
lines.english: “Sorry. I shouldn’t have pried.”

lines.japanese: 軽く頭を下げると、紀奈子さんは俺の背中をぽんと優しく叩いてくれました。うーんしまった、我ながら失敗だったなあ。
lines.english: I bowed my head, and Kinako gave me a gentle pat on the back. Damn. I'd really put my foot in it.

lines.japanese: 「いいのいいの。実質的には私、それほど苦労してないんだ。おばあちゃんたちが資金援助してくれてるから」
lines.english: “It's all right. Materially, I haven't had it too hard. Grandma and the others help me with money.”

lines.japanese: 実質的にはって言った。精神的には結構つらいんじゃないかなあ。
lines.english: She had said *materially*. Emotionally, it must have been another story.

lines.japanese: 「そんなわけだから、私に三浪目はないの。今年で本当に最後の最後」
lines.english: “So this is it for me. I don't get another year. This really is my last chance.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「今回で駄目だったら進学あきらめるって、そういう約束でおばあちゃんたちにお金貸してもらったから」
lines.english: “Grandma and the others lent me the money on the condition that if I fail this time, I give up on university.”

lines.japanese: 「中立派のお母さんからもたまに電話くるけど、喧嘩ばっかりでもう疲れちゃった。受験校のレベル下げたほうがいいとか、滑り止めをもっと増やせとか、私が何ヵ月もかけて出した結論にすぐケチつけるんだもん」
lines.english: “Mom calls sometimes too, since she's neutral, but I'm tired of fighting every time. She tells me to aim for easier schools or apply to more safeties. It took me months to make these decisions, and she finds fault with them in seconds.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……えでも、それって紀奈子さんを心配してのことなんすよね？」
lines.english: “I see… But she says those things because she’s worried about you, doesn’t she?”
“Yes…”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それは分かってるの。でもこっちも、落ちることが前提の話はしたくないとか、お母さんにはお金借りてないんだから黙っててほしいとか、いろいろ意地になっちゃって」
lines.english: “Yes, I know. But then I get stubborn too. I tell her I don't want every conversation to assume I'm going to fail, and that since I didn't borrow the money from her, she should stay out of it.”

lines.japanese: 「言いあってるときは気付かないし、気付いてもやっぱり譲れない部分はあるんだよね。せっかく電話もらっても、結局いつも最後には衝突しちゃうんさぁ」
lines.english: “In the middle of an argument, I can't see what I'm doing. Even when I can, there are things I still can't back down on. Mom goes to the trouble of calling, and somehow we always end up fighting again.”

lines.japanese: 「はあー、早く合格して望月家の問題児を卒業したいよ。今のままじゃ、お父さんに謝る権利すらないし」
lines.english: “I just want to pass and graduate from being the Mochizuki family problem child. As things stand, I haven't even earned the right to apologize to Dad.”

lines.japanese: 言葉がありません。家族なんて羨ましいものを持たない俺には、彼女の苦悩が重いのか軽いのかさえ分かりません。
lines.english: I had no words. I'd never had that enviable thing called a family, so I couldn't even tell whether her anguish was heavy or light.

lines.japanese: でもひとつ気付いたことがありました。
lines.english: But I did realize one thing.

lines.japanese: このひとはたぶん俺と同類だ。このひとの柔らかで温かな笑顔は、見せたくない素顔を隠すための仮面だ。
lines.english: She was probably one of my kind. Her soft, warm smile was a mask for the face she did not want anyone to see.

lines.japanese: 俺やマスターと同じで、格好悪い自分をごまかすために笑っている弱いひとなんだ。
lines.english: Like the boss and me, she was weak enough to laugh so no one would see the parts of herself she found shameful.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、受かるといっすねえ、ははは」
lines.english: “Well, I sure hope you pass. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 陳腐な励ましとともに、へらへら笑ってあげました。
lines.english: I gave her a foolish grin and the most commonplace encouragement imaginable.

lines.japanese: 観衆に笑ってもらうのが道化の報酬だってことぐらい、俺は誰よりも知っています。慰撫や同情なんてノーサンキューです。
lines.english: No one knew better than I that an audience's laughter was the clown's reward. Comfort and pity? No, thank you.

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、話しちゃった」
lines.english: “Hee hee. I went and told you everything.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「千歳くんは話を聞くの上手だね。それって一つの才能だと思うよ」
lines.english: “You're a good listener, Chitose. I think that's a talent in itself.”

lines.japanese: 「そっすかあ？」
lines.english: “You really think so?”

lines.japanese: 嬉しいこと言ってくださる。
lines.english: What a lovely thing to say.

lines.japanese: 「えりちゃんは飽きたって言って聞いてくれないし、お店の他のひとには話そうと思わなかったし、千歳君に聞いてもらったのが久しぶりだよ」
lines.english: “Eri says she's heard it all before and won't listen anymore. I never felt like telling anyone else at the restaurant. It's been a long time since I had someone hear me out.”

lines.japanese: 「楽になりました？」
lines.english: “Do you feel better?”

lines.japanese: 「ぜんぜん！　これから帰ってまたケンカしてくるさ！」
lines.english: “Not at all! I'm going home to have another fight!”

lines.japanese: 「うわっ！　俺の存在価値、薄っ！」
lines.english: “What!? So much for my value as a human being!”

lines.japanese: 俺と紀奈子さんはけらけら笑いながら大通りを歩きました。
lines.english: Kinako and I walked down the main street, laughing together.

lines.japanese: 「千歳君」
lines.english: “Chitose.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「また私の話聞いてね」
lines.english: “Listen to me again sometime.”

lines.japanese: 「機会があれば」
lines.english: “If the opportunity arises.”

lines.japanese: 俺は笑顔で答えました。
lines.english: I answered with a smile.

lines.japanese: がんばれ同志。道化から道化へ、スマイル・フォー・ユー。
lines.english: Hang in there, comrade. From one clown to another—a smile for you.

lines.japanese: 「よーし、じゃあ今日はもう仕方ないから、明日から勉強がんばるぞー！」
lines.english: “All right! It can't be helped today, so I'll start studying hard tomorrow!”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さん……」
lines.english: “Kinako…”

lines.japanese: それ毎日言ってますよね……。
lines.english: You say that every day.

lines.japanese: マジで頑張ってくれよオイ。
lines.english: Please. I mean it. Start studying.

lines.japanese: 紀奈子さんが向かいのビルのトイレで着替えを済ませたあと、俺たちはすぐに占いの館『柳木原の叔母』へ向かいました。
lines.english: After Kinako changed in the restroom of the building across the street, we headed straight for the fortune-telling parlor, the Auntie of Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: エレベーターを出るとそこにはそこそこ雰囲気のある厳めしいホールが広がっていて、タキシードを着た店員さんに受付まで案内されました。
lines.english: The elevator opened onto an imposing hall that managed a respectable air of mystery, and an attendant in a tuxedo showed us to reception.

lines.japanese: ネットで拝見したと言ってブルボンヌ冴子先生を指名。幸いお客さんが入っていなかったらしく、すぐに彼女の部屋へ案内してもらうことが出来ました。
lines.english: I told the receptionist I had found them online and asked for Madame Saeko Bourbonne. Fortunately, she had no client at the time, and we were shown straight to her room.

lines.japanese: 「千歳くん千歳くん、ぜんぜん打ち合わせしてないけどいいの？」
lines.english: “Chitose, Chitose. We haven’t planned this at all. Are you sure we’ll be all right?”

lines.japanese: 「我々は役者さんじゃありません、下手に考えておくと発言が芝居臭くなります。ノープラン・オンリーワンテイクの出たとこ勝負で行きましょう」
lines.english: “We aren't actors. If we plan too much, everything we say will sound rehearsed. No plan, one take. We improvise.”

lines.japanese: 「相手のことはある程度ブログで調べてあります。俺が主導で話を進めるので、紀奈子さんは隣りでテキトーに相槌だけ打っててください」
lines.english: “I've learned a fair amount about her from the blog. I'll lead the conversation. Kinako, just sit beside me and make the right noises.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、わかった」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 俺たちはホールに比べて安っぽい作りの扉を開けて、占い師のいる部屋へと入りました。
lines.english: We opened a cheaply made door that contrasted sharply with the hall and entered the fortune-teller's room.

lines.japanese: 「ようこそ、神龍の間へ……」
lines.english: “Welcome... to the Chamber of Shenron.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、どーもどーもお世話さまですコンバンワ～。元気？　平和？　青春？　はいはい、俺は元気ですよ平和ですよ青春ですよ！」
lines.english: “Hello, hello! Evening! How are we? Happy? Peaceful? Young and thriving? Me, I'm great, I'm peaceful, and positively blooming!”

lines.japanese: ハイテンションモードのスイッチを入れた俺に、アラビアンな民族衣装の占術士さんが訝しげな目を向けました。
lines.english: The diviner in Arabian costume gave me a suspicious look as I flipped the switch on my high-energy persona.

lines.japanese: しかし俺は知っています。彼女は会社でのインテリ風なイメージとは裏腹に、本性はスイーツ大好き流行りもの大好きな普通ぅーのミーハーお姉さんなのです。
lines.english: But I knew the truth. Beneath the intellectual image she projected at the office, she was an ordinary, trend-chasing young woman who adored sweets and whatever happened to be fashionable.

lines.japanese: そして彼女のマイブームは、ホットヨガとお笑い。前者は効果が表れずぼちぼち飽き気味ですが、後者はまさに今がピーク。新人芸人のライブなんかにも足繁く通うほどの入れ込みっぷりです。
lines.english: Her current obsessions were hot yoga and comedy. The former had produced no visible results and was beginning to bore her. Her passion for the latter, however, was at its peak. She even frequented live shows by rookie comedians.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、騒がしなってスンマセン。営業の帰りやもんで、ついテンションおかしなってもうてん。あ、ぼくまだ駆け出しやねんけど、ちょいちょい芸人やっとるんですわ」
lines.english: “Sorry for the noise. I'm just back from a gig and I'm still a little wired. I'm only starting out, but I do comedy here and there.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、なんて芸名……あ、失礼しました。どうぞ、まずはお掛けください」
lines.english: “Oh! What's your stage na— My apologies. Please, sit down first.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、よろしゅ頼んますー」
lines.english: “Thanks for having us.”

lines.japanese: 「ますー」
lines.english: “Having us.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、よろしくお願いします」
lines.english: “Yes. Thank you.”

lines.japanese: 非日常的なコスプレ衣装をまとってはいますが、以前祥玄社でお会いした沢井冴子さんそのひとに間違いありません。薄いベールが下りているその奥に、フレームのない眼鏡が光っていました。
lines.english: Despite the fantastical costume, she was unmistakably Saeko Sawai, whom I had met at Shogensha. Rimless glasses glinted behind her thin veil.

lines.japanese: ふわっと鼻をつくのは、米田さんが教えてくれた香水の香り。俺の隣りでは、制服姿の紀奈子さんがひたすらニコニコしていました。
lines.english: A waft of the perfume Yoneda had told me about reached my nose. Beside me, Kinako sat in her school uniform, smiling and smiling.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　あなたどこかで……？」
lines.english: “Hmm? Have I seen you somewhere…?”

lines.japanese: 沢井さんが俺の面相をしげしげ眺めます。編集部で一度お会いしてることは、すっかり覚えておられない御様子。これは好都合。
lines.english: Sawai studied my face intently. Apparently she had completely forgotten our single meeting at the editorial office. Excellent.

lines.japanese: 「エッ！　ほんま、覚えててくらはったんですか！　そうです、先月このお店のイベントで『客席ランダム☆占ってドン』やったとき、ぼくその２０人の中のひとりやったんです」
lines.english: “What! You really remembered me? That's right. Last month, when this place held that ‘Random Audience Member Fortune-Telling Bonanza,’ I was one of the twenty people you picked.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、そうでしたか。道理で見覚え──」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes, of course. I knew your face looked—”

lines.japanese: 「──失敬。それではまず、お名前から教えてください」
lines.english: “—forgive me. First, may I have your names?”

lines.japanese: 「成田隼人です」
lines.english: “Hayato Narita.”

lines.japanese: 「望月タバス子です」
lines.english: “Tabasco Mochizuki.”

lines.japanese: 「ナリタハヤト……？　聞いたことない芸人ね、どこの事務所かしら。それともまだ養成所生？」
lines.english: “Hayato Narita...? I've never heard of a comedian by that name. Which agency is he with? Or is he still in training?”

lines.japanese: 「あのー、冴子センセ？」
lines.english: “Um, Madame Saeko?”

lines.japanese: 「センセ？」
lines.english: “Madame?”

lines.japanese: 「失敬。えー、それで今日は何の御相談で」
lines.english: “Forgive me. Now, what brings you here today?”

lines.japanese: 「せやねえ。ほんだらもうすぐタバス子の受験やん、学業運でも占ってもろたらええ」
lines.english: “Well, Tabasco's entrance exams are coming up, so perhaps you could take a look at her academic prospects.”

lines.japanese: 「もろたらええ」
lines.english: “Take a look.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。仲がよろしいんですね」
lines.english: “I see. You two seem very close.”

lines.japanese: 「私たち、まだ付きあって三日目なんです」
lines.english: “This is only our third day together.”

lines.japanese: いや、紀奈子さんあの、余計なアドリブいらないから……てかその訛り、どこ弁？
lines.english: Kinako, I didn't need the extra improvisation... And what part of the country was that accent even supposed to be from?

lines.japanese: 「かしこまりました。それでは手相から拝見させていただきます。男性の方、お手を」
lines.english: “Very well. Let us begin by examining your palms. Sir, your hand, please.”

lines.japanese: 「お願いします」
lines.english: “Here you are.”

lines.japanese: 「あら、仕事線が長いですね。近いうちブレイクするかもしれませんよ」
lines.english: “My, your career line is long. You may have your big break very soon.”

lines.japanese: 「まじで！」
lines.english: “Seriously!?”

lines.japanese: 思わず素で喜んでしまいました。これから新人ライター千歳鷲介がめきめき頭角を表すということでしょうか。いやあ、見る目ありますねブルボンヌ先生。
lines.english: I forgot myself and lit up. Did this mean rookie writer Shusuke Chitose was about to burst onto the scene? Madame Bourbonne certainly knew talent when she saw it.

lines.japanese: なんて浮かれてる場合じゃない。本来の目的を果たさねば。
lines.english: This was no time to get carried away. I had a real objective to accomplish.

lines.japanese: 「それでは画数、星座、手相などから結果を割りだします。しばしお待ちのほどを。むむぅ……」
lines.english: “I shall derive your result from the number of strokes in your names, your astrological signs, your palms, and other factors. Please wait a moment. Mmm...”

lines.japanese: 沢井さんがなにやら水晶球とにらめっこを始めたので、その隙に俺は例の文庫本を取りだしました。
lines.english: Sawai began staring intently into a crystal ball. While her attention was occupied, I drew out the paperback in question.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、せやタバス子、いまのうちにコレ」
lines.english: “Oh, right, Tabasco. Here—take this while we wait.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　これなんだい？」
lines.english: “Hmm? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「アホ、こないだ言うたやん。その本、いま芸人仲間のあいだでめっちゃ流行っとんねん。おもろいだけやナシに、文章ごっつ綺麗やから、受験対策で活字慣れしとくにも丁度ええカンジやで」
lines.english: “Dummy, I told you the other day. This book is huge with all my comedian friends right now. It isn't just funny—the prose is gorgeous. Perfect for getting used to reading before your exams.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっか言ってたねー。へー、これどこの本？　んーと、しょう、げん、しゃ？」
lines.english: “Oh, right. You did tell me. Who published it? Let’s see… Sho-gen-sha?”

lines.japanese: 「あの」
lines.english: “Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: 目を閉じて精神統一していたはずのブルボンヌ先生が、案の定ぱちりと目蓋を開きました。
lines.english: Madame Bourbonne, who was supposed to be meditating with her eyes closed, opened them right on cue.

lines.japanese: 「いまそちらの御本から興味深い波動を感じました。よろしければ拝見させていただいても？」
lines.english: “I sensed an intriguing vibration from that book. If you would permit me to examine it?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、かめへんですよ」
lines.english: “Sure, be my guest.”

lines.japanese: 「細川玉木の『米寿』ですよ」
lines.english: “It’s *Eighty-Eight*, by Tamaki Hosokawa.”

lines.japanese: 「細河田マキ？　うちで関わってる作家にそんな人……いたような、いないような……」
lines.english: “Maki Hosokawada? Do we publish someone by that name...? I feel as though we might. Or might not...”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、センセ知ったはるんですか！　まあ、細川ちゃん一作目は大ヒットしてますもんねえ。ふだん小説読まれへんやつらにもめっちゃ人気ですからね」
lines.english: “Oh! You know her, Madame? Well, Tamaki Hosokawa's first book was a huge hit. She's wildly popular even with people who never read novels.”

lines.japanese: 「細川玉木なら、うちのガッコでもみんな知ってるよー」
lines.english: “Everybody at my school knows Tamaki Hosokawa.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ……細河田マキ……担当はうちの誰かしら」
lines.english: “Really… Maki Hosokawada… I wonder who handles her at our office.”

lines.japanese: <8>\「え！　センセまさかご存知ない！」
lines.english: “What! You mean you don’t know her!?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、そんな……この店の占い師さんはみんな流行に敏感って聞いてきたのに……」
lines.english: “Oh, no... We heard all the fortune-tellers here were up on the latest trends...”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえっ？　存じてますよ、もちろん知ってますわよ。細河田マキでしょ。祥玄社さんには美人で優秀な社員が多いって噂だから、売れたのは版元の力も大きかったんじゃないかしら」
lines.english: “I-I do know her! Of course I know Maki Hosokawada. Shogensha is rumored to employ many beautiful and gifted people, so surely the publisher deserves much of the credit for her success.”

lines.japanese: とか言いながら、明らかに何かを思いだそうとしている表情の沢井さん。
lines.english: Even as she spoke, Sawai was visibly racking her brain.

lines.japanese: よし、ここで伝家の宝刀。沢井さんの日記にしばしば登場する、彼女にとってナンバーワン・フェイバリット芸人コンビ『楽しい中耳炎』さんの名前をお借りしちゃいましょう。
lines.english: Excellent. Time to draw my secret weapon. I would borrow the name of Sawai's absolute favorite comedy duo, fixtures of her online diary: Happy Otitis Media.

lines.japanese: 「せや、知ってっかタバス子。細川玉木ゆーたらアレやで、タノチューの耳ダレにいさんも、いまめっちゃドハマリしよってん」
lines.english: “Oh, Tabasco, you know what? Ear Drip from Happy O.M. is completely hooked on Tamaki Hosokawa right now.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ！　うせやん！？」
lines.english: “What! No way!?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ほんまですよ。モノ見る目ぇ肥えてはるあのひとが、細川玉木だけはぜったい来るーゆうてはりますからね」
lines.english: “It's true. A man with taste as refined as his says Tamaki Hosokawa is absolutely going to be the next big thing.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ダレさんがそこまで……？」
lines.english: “Ear Drip said that much…?”

lines.japanese: 「細川玉木もよう知らん女は眼鏡かける資格ないでー、とも言ってた」
lines.english: “He also said any woman who doesn't know Tamaki Hosokawa has no right to wear glasses.”
“Seriously!?”

lines.japanese: 「そらそうですわ、一度読んでもろたら分かります。細川玉木、細川玉木、ぼくのわたしの細川玉木をよろしくお願いいたします」
lines.english: “Of course. Read her once and you'll understand. Tamaki Hosokawa! Tamaki Hosokawa! Please show your support for everyone's beloved Tamaki Hosokawa!”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、俺とタバス子が付きあい始めたきっかけも細川玉木やもんね。そらしゃあないで。そらあ男やったら誰だって、街角で細川玉木読んでる女にはつい声かけてまうやろ」
lines.english: “Why, Tamaki Hosokawa is how Tabasco and I got together. Couldn't be helped. Any man would strike up a conversation if he saw a woman reading Tamaki Hosokawa on a street corner.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなの！？　え、そんな出会いまであるの？」
lines.english: “Really!? People even meet that way?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、何それ！　メモっとこ、ほそ、細河田マキ……っと」
lines.english: “Wait, what is this? I need to write it down. Maki... Hoso... kawada...”

lines.japanese: 「センセ、細川玉木です」
lines.english: “Madame, it’s Tamaki Hosokawa.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ああ、知ってるわよ。ふん、細川玉木でしょ。細川……ん、それもしかして私の担当じゃない？　あれ、どうだったかな、あとで帰ったら調べとこ」
lines.english: “Oh, yes, I know. Hmph. Tamaki Hosokawa. Hosokawa... Wait, isn't she one of mine? Hmm. I can't remember. I'll look it up when I get home.”

lines.japanese: よしよし、いいです、いい感じです。
lines.english: Good, good. This was going beautifully.

lines.japanese: 彼女が細川玉木の最新作『いつだってプリズム』に目を通す確率は、これで多少上がったんじゃないでしょうか。
lines.english: Surely the odds that she would read Tamaki Hosokawa's latest work, *Always a Prism*, had risen somewhat.

lines.japanese: 「千歳くん千歳くん、上手くいったっぽいね？」
lines.english: “Chitose, Chitose. I think it worked.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、おかげさまで。じゃあそろそろ帰りましょうか」
lines.english: “Yes, thanks to you. Shall we be going, then?”

lines.japanese: 俺と紀奈子さんは顔を見合わせて微笑みました。
lines.english: Kinako and I exchanged smiles.

lines.japanese: 「……えー、大変お待たせしました。結果が出ました」
lines.english: “…Thank you for your patience. I have the result.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: もう気持ちが半ば帰るモードになっていた俺と紀奈子さんは、突然かけられた声にきょとんとしました。
lines.english: Kinako and I were already halfway out the door mentally, so the sudden announcement left us staring blankly.

lines.japanese: ああそういえば占いの途中でしたね。客として来た以上は、怪しまれないように一応最後まで聞いておいた方がいいでしょう。
lines.english: Oh, right. We were in the middle of a fortune-telling session. Since we had come as customers, we ought to stay for the result rather than arouse suspicion.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そんだら聞かせてください」
lines.english: “Sure, let’s hear it.”

lines.japanese: 「はい。望月パスタ子さんの勉強運は……」
lines.english: “Very well. Miss Pasta Mochizuki's academic fortune is...”

lines.japanese: 「勉強運は？」
lines.english: “My academic fortune is?”

lines.japanese: 「こちらの男性と共に過ごすほど運気が上がります！」
lines.english: “Your luck will rise the more time you spend with this gentleman!”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: <8>\「ええええっ！」
lines.english: “Whaaaat!?”

lines.japanese: とつぜん大声を出す紀奈子さん。占いぐらいで大袈裟ですが、まだ演技を続けてるんでしょうか。
lines.english: Kinako suddenly cried out. That seemed a little dramatic for a fortune. Was she still acting?

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうしよう千歳君……私、千歳君と一緒にいれば合格するって……」
lines.english: “Wh-what should I do, Chitose? She says I'll pass if I stay with you...”

lines.japanese: 「いや、信じてどうするんすか。ていうか照れないでくださいよ」
lines.english: “Why would you believe her? And please don't start blushing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん、だよね、信じてるわけじゃないんだけど、いきなり言われてびっくりしちゃった」
lines.english: “Oh. Right, of course. I don’t believe it. I was only surprised to hear it out of nowhere.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみにおふたりは恋愛運も良好ですよ。相性は最高です。お互いこれ以上の伴侶はないでしょう」
lines.english: “Your romantic fortunes are also excellent. Your compatibility could not be better. Neither of you will ever find a more suitable companion.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ほんとに……」
lines.english: “Is that really true…?”

lines.japanese: 「や、だから紀奈子さん、信じないでってば。だいたい、うちらが名乗ったのは偽名でしょう。しかもタバス子だっつってんのに、冴子センセいまパスタ子とか言ってましたよ。ぜんぜん信用できませんって」
lines.english: “Kinako, I told you not to believe her. We gave her false names in the first place. And after we said *Tabasco*, Madame Saeko just called you *Pasta*. She has no credibility at all.”

lines.japanese: 「うう、そうは言うけど……どうしよ、ひよちゃんに受験の日まで千歳君貸してもらおうかな……」
lines.english: “I know, but... What should I do? Maybe I should ask Hiyo to lend me Chitose until the exam...”

lines.japanese: 「試験当日は恋人に会場まで送ってもらうといいでしょう」
lines.english: “On the day of the examination, have your lover accompany you to the testing site.”

lines.japanese: 「千歳君、来てくれる……？」
lines.english: “Chitose… will you come?”
“What!?”

lines.japanese: どこまで本気で言ってるんでしょう。乞うような目で見つめられて、俺はついうっかり「もちろん！」などと答えそうになってしまいました。
lines.english: How serious was she? She gazed at me with pleading eyes, and I nearly blurted out, “Of course!”

lines.japanese: いや、いやダメ！　仮にも告白して返事待ちの身なんだから、ふらふらしちゃダメ！
lines.english: No, no! I couldn't! I had confessed to someone and was still waiting for her answer. I could not let myself waver!
“You won’t…?”

lines.japanese: ああでも紀奈子さん可愛いなあ。
lines.english: Ah, but Kinako was so adorable.

lines.japanese: <10>\　ってダメえぇぇぇー！
lines.english: Noooo! Absolutely not!

lines.japanese: 「冴子先生、僕の邪念を祓ってください」
lines.english: “Madame Saeko, please exorcise my impure thoughts.”
